stem: Commonest tumors of the central nervous system arise from
explanation: Most CNS tumors = gliomas -> arise from neuroglial cells (astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma, ependymoma). Glioblastoma multiforme -> most common primary malignant brain tumor. Why others are incorrect: (A) Meningiomas -> common benign extra-axial tumors, not intrinsic CNS tumors. (C) Blood vessels: Hemangioblastomas - rare. (D) Nerve cells: Neuronal tumors are rare (e.g. neurocytoma). Related info: Primary brain tumors in adults: gliomas > meningiomas > schwannomas. Children: Medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Clearance of drug depends on
explanation: Clearance (CL) = Vd x 0.693 / t1/2. Other options: b) Bioavailability affects oral dose not clearance. c) Diffusion coefficient -> less relevant. d) Rate of absorption -> affects Tmax, not clearance. Key point: Clearance determines steady-state levels of drug.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Plasma albumin helps in
explanation: Colloidal osmotic pressure maintenance: Maintains oncotic pressure to prevent edema. Other options: b) Blood clotting: Role of fibrinogen, not albumin. c) Iron transport: Done by transferrin. d) Copper transport: Done by ceruloplasmin.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: The followings are mainly intracellular parasites
explanation: Leishmania donovani -> obligate intracellular parasite, survives inside macrophages. Causes visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar). Why others are incorrect: (A) Echinococcus granulosus: Extracellular cyst in liver, lung - not intracellular. (C) Trypanosoma gambiense: Mostly extracellular in blood and lymph. (D) COVID RNA virus. Related info: Other intracellular parasites: Toxoplasma gondii, Plasmodium spp., Leishmania spp., Trypanosoma cruzi (partially).

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Which of the following hormones exhibits a diurnal rhythm in its secretion
explanation: ACTH peaks in the early morning -> diurnal pattern. Other options: b), (C), (D): No true diurnal secretion. Key point: Cortisol & ACTH both show circadian rhythm.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Which among the following is protozoal infection
explanation: Giardiasis is caused by Giardia lamblia, a protozoan parasite infecting the gastrointestinal tract. Other options: b) Schistosomiasis -> caused by trematode (fluke) worms. c) Filariasis -> caused by nematode worms (filarial worms). d) Hydatid disease -> caused by cestode (tapeworm)

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Spores are killed by
options: Moist heat at 110 Celsius for 30 minutes 42nd Special BCS
explanation: Spores are resistant - killed by moist heat (autoclave) at 110-121 Celsius.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Vitamin K is necessary for synthesis of
explanation: Vitamin K -> required for gamma-carboxylation of factors II (prothrombin), VII, IX, X. Key point: Warfarin -> vitamin K antagonist -> increases bleeding risk.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Linear growth is determined by
explanation: IGF-1 mediates the effects of growth hormone on chondrocyte proliferation and bone elongation -> key regulator of linear growth. Other options: (A, B, C) Minerals and vitamin D are essential for bone mineralization but do not primarily regulate growth plate activity. childhood and adolescence. Key point: IGF-1 is crucial for longitudinal bone growth during.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: A stretch reflex is
explanation: Stretch reflex (e.g. knee jerk) -> monosynaptic -> direct connection between afferent & efferent neurons. Other options: b) Polysynaptic -> more complex reflexes. c) Initiated by muscle spindle -> true,d) Mainly via type Ia, not type II. Key point: Fastest reflex arc -> monosynaptic.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Umbilical cord contains
explanation: Umbilical cord contains 2 arteries, 1 vein -> correct answer is “One umbilical vein”. Other options: a): Actually two arteries. Key point: Vein carries oxygenated blood from placenta to fetus.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Deep cervical fascia encloses
explanation: The pretracheal layer of deep cervical fascia encloses the thyroid gland, trachea, and esophagus. Other options: a) Larynx -> surrounded by membranes, not deep fascia. c) Pineal gland -> inside brain, not neck fascia. d) Submandibular -> enclosed by superficial fascia. planes. Key point: Important: infection can spread along cervical fascia.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: In Graves’ disease, one would least likely expect
explanation: TSH is low in Graves’ disease (due to negative feedback). Why others are incorrect: (A) Goitre -> present. (B) increased BMR -> hyperthyroid state. (D) Weight loss -> common. Graves: TSH low, T3/T4 high, TSI +ve.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Complete destruction of zona glomerulosa result in unable to produce
explanation: Zona glomerulosa -> aldosterone (mineralocorticoid). Why others are incorrect: (A) Adrenaline -> adrenal medulla. (C) Cortisol -> zona fasciculata. (D) DHEA -> zona reticularis. Layers: G -> Aldosterone F -> Cortisol R -> Androgens.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: The diaphragm is pierced by
explanation: Phrenic nerves (left and right) pierce the diaphragm to provide its motor innervation. Other options: a) Sympathetic trunk -> lies posteriorly, does not pierce diaphragm. b) Lowest intercostal nerves -> supply abdominal muscles. d) Pudendal nerve -> supplies perineum Key point: Phrenic nerve originates from C3-C5.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: A major sign of cardiac tamponade is
explanation: Pulsus paradoxus (decreased BP on inspiration) -> classic tamponade sign. Other options: a) Bradycardia -> not typical. b) Ventricular dilatation -> not possible due to compression. Tamponade = Beck’s triad: decreased BP , muffled heart sounds, increased JVP .

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Renal control of acid base balance is a function of
explanation: The distal tubule & collecting duct are key sites for H+ secretion and HCO3- reabsorption -> acid-base regulation. Other options: a) Loop of Henle -> concentration of urine, not acid- base balance. b) Proximal tubule -> reabsorbs bulk of HCO3- but distal tubule fine-tunes pH. d) Glomerulus -> filtration, no active pH regulation. Distal nephron = important in compensating for acidosis/alkalosis.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Blood brain barrier formed by
explanation: Endothelial cells of CNS capillaries with tight junctions form the BBB. Why others are incorrect: (B) Ependyma -> lines ventricles; (C) Oligodendrocytes -> make myelin. (D) Epithelial cells -> not in capillary wall. BBB prevents large or charged molecules, protects brain from toxins.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Substance that can easily diffuse through
explanation: Oxygen = small, nonpolar -> diffuses easily through lipid bilayer. Other options: a) Glucose -> large, needs transporters. c) Na+ -> needs channels. Key point: Lipid-soluble & small gases diffuse easily (O2, CO2).

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: In aerobic exercise there is decrease in
explanation: Sweating -> plasma volume decreased during prolonged exercise. Other options: b) Skin temp increased (vasodilation). c) CBF maintained or slightly increased. d) Mean BP increased slightly. Key point: Plasma volume decreased -> need hydration during exercise.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: A regurgitant aortic valve in a non functioning heart causes
explanation: Aortic regurgitation -> backflow during diastole -> decreased diastolic pressure -> widened pulse pressure. Why others are incorrect: (B) HR is compensatory increased, not decreased. (C) Diastolic murmur in AR, not systolic. (D) Systolic BP is usually increased or normal due to increased stroke volume. AR murmur: Early diastolic, decrescendo, best heard at LSB.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Pyramidine bases are catabolised to
explanation: Pyrimidine breakdown -> beta-alanine, CO2, and NH3 (ammonia). Other options: a) Orotic acid -> intermediate in synthesis, not catabolism. b) Uric acid -> from purines. c) Valproic acid -> unrelated drug.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: The major function of surfactant is to increase
explanation: Surfactant reduces surface tension -> improves pulmonary compliance -> makes lung expansion easier. Other options: a) It decreases, not increases, surface tension. c) Decreases work of breathing. d) Prevents, not promotes, lung collapse (atelectasis). Key point: Produced by type II pneumocytes.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Local blood vessels are dilated due to increased concentration of
explanation: increased Potassium causes vasodilation by relaxing vascular smooth muscle. Other options: a) Endothelin -> vasoconstrictor. b) Sodium -> no direct vasodilatory effect. c) Calcium -> vasoconstriction.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: In emphysema, pulmonary function test shows
explanation: Emphysema -> hyperinflation -> increased total lung capacity (TLC), increased RV . Other options: a) RV increased not decreased. b) FEV1/FVC decreased due to airflow limitation. d) VC is usually decreased or normal. Key point: Classic PFT: decreased FEV1/FVC, increased TLC, increased RV .

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Medial trunk of brachial plexus gives rise to
explanation: The medial cord of the brachial plexus (not “trunk”) gives rise to the medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm. The medial cord is formed from the anterior division of the lower trunk (C8-T1). Why others are incorrect: (A) Radial nerve arises from the posterior cord (C5- T1). (C) Axillary nerve arises from the posterior cord (C5- C6). Related info: Brachial plexus cords: Lateral, medial, posterior. Major branches from medial cord: Medial pectoral, medial cutaneous nerve of arm, medial cutaneous nerve of forearm, ulnar nerve, part of median nerve.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Rickets radiology
explanation: Rickets -> defective mineralization -> widening of growth plate (epiphysis). Other options: a) Cupping seen but widening more diagnostic. b), (D): Not typical findings. Key point: Widened epiphysis = classic sign in active rickets.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: In which poisoning gastric lavage is contraindicated
explanation: Kerosene (a hydrocarbon) poisoning -> gastric lavage is contraindicated due to high risk of aspiration pneumonitis. Other options: a) OPC -> lavage may be used early with airway protection. c) Paracetamol -> lavage within 1 hour can be considered.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Regarding Ionizing radiation-following is true
explanation: Ionizing radiation affects all tissues - including the brain - especially in children (brain more radiosensitive). Risk: CNS necrosis, cognitive deficits. Why others are incorrect: (A) Age matters - younger tissues are more radiosensitive. (B) Lungs are sensitive -> radiation pneumonitis, fibrosis. (C) Skin is highly sensitive -> dermatitis, atrophy. Related info: Most radiosensitive: Bone marrow, gonads, gut mucosa. Radioresistant: Cartilage, muscle. Late effects: Fibrosis, malignancy, vascular damage.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Which of the followings are unencapsulated receptor
explanation: Merkel’s disc -> unencapsulated, slow-adapting touch receptor (pressure, texture). Why others are incorrect: (A) Ruffini -> encapsulated. (C) Pacinian -> encapsulated, deep pressure/vibration. (D) Meissner’s -> encapsulated, light touch. Other unencapsulated: Free nerve endings, hair follicle receptors.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Which of the following does not have a membrane
explanation: Ribosomes = no membrane - consist of rRNA + protein. Why others are incorrect: (B) Mitochondria -> double membrane. (C) Nucleus -> double membrane (nuclear envelope). (D) Chloroplast -> double membrane.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Cerebellar lesion causes
explanation: Intention tremor occurs during purposeful movement due to cerebellar dysfunction affecting coordination. Other options: a) Spasticity and (B) Rigidity -> features of upper motor neuron and extrapyramidal disorders respectively. d) Slow gait -> nonspecific, cerebellar ataxia causes unsteady gait rather than slow. intention tremor.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Retroperitoneal structures include
explanation: Ascending colon = secondarily retroperitoneal. Why others are incorrect: (A) Transverse colon -> intraperitoneal. (C) IVC -> retroperitoneal but not an option matching colon question. (D) Appendix -> intraperitoneal. Retroperitoneal mnemonic: SAD PUCKER.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Hot air oven is used for sterilization
explanation: Swab stick -> dry heat sterilization in hot air oven. Other options: a), (B), (C) -> usually autoclave (moist heat) or flame. labile items).

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Bleeding time is Prolonged in
explanation: Von Willebrand disease -> platelet adhesion defect -> prolonged bleeding time. Other options: a) ITP -> thrombocytopenia causes prolonged bleeding time, but more severe cases; (D) Haemophilia A and B -> coagulation factor deficiencies -> normal bleeding time but prolonged clotting time. coagulation cascade. Key point: Bleeding time reflects platelet function.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Biochemical disturbance occurs in fulminating hepatic failure is
explanation: Acute liver failure -> decreased synthesis of clotting factors -> prolonged prothrombin time, a sensitive marker of liver synthetic function. Other options: a) Metabolic alkalosis -> uncommon; usually metabolic acidosis occurs. b) Hypoglycemia -> can occur but less consistent. c) High serum albumin -> albumin decreases due to synthetic failure. liver failure. Key point: PT prolongation is a critical prognostic factor in acute. Liver failure

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: In Addison’s disease, there is
explanation: Addison’s -> cortisol deficiency -> fasting hypoglycemia due to impaired gluconeogenesis. Other options: a) Low, not high cortisol. b) Hypotension occurs. d) Hyperpigmentation (not hypo) from increased ACTH. ACTH. 42nd Special BCS

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Mood stabilizer is
explanation: Lithium is a classic mood stabilizer used in bipolar disorder. Key point: Lithium = gold standard for mood stabilization.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Vit K
explanation: Vitamin K is utilized in the liver for the synthesis of clotting factors (II, VII, IX, X). Other options: b) Synthesized by gut bacteria, not intestinal epithelium

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Pancreatitis causes of elevation of plasma
explanation: Plasma lipase is elevated in acute pancreatitis - more specific than amylase. Why others are incorrect: (B) Aldolase -> muscle/liver disease. Diagnostic enzymes: Lipase: rises earlier, stays elevated longer than amylase.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Causes of high ESR is
explanation: Multiple myeloma -> increased ESR due to high immunoglobulins. Other options: a) Polycythemia -> decreased ESR. b) Sickle cell -> decreased ESR. d) Spherocytosis -> not marked ESR change. High ESR = inflammation, infection, myeloma.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Excitatory cells of nervous system includes
options: Anterior horn cells of spinal cord
explanation: Anterior horn cells are motor neurons that send excitatory signals to skeletal muscles -> key excitatory neurons. Other options: b) Ependymal cells -> line ventricles, involved in CSF production. c) Microglia -> immune cells of CNS, not excitatory. d) Purkinje cells -> inhibitory neurons in cerebellum, not excitatory. for muscle contraction.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: In basal condition, most of the energy used by cardiac muscle from metabolism of
explanation: At rest -> 70-80% energy from fatty acids. Why others are incorrect: (B) Glucose -> minor role at rest. . (D) Pyruvate -> intermediate, not major source. During stress/exercise -> glucose & lactate increased.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Content of the broad ligament
explanation: The ovarian artery runs within the suspensory ligament, a part of the broad ligament, supplying blood to the ovary. Other options: a) Testes -> male gonads, not in female broad ligament. b) Ovary -> suspended by mesovarium, not enclosed within broad ligament. c) Ureter -> retroperitoneal, crosses under uterine artery, but not a content of broad ligament. lymphatics supplying female reproductive organs.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: X-linked disorder is
explanation: Haemophilia (A & B) -> X-linked recessive disorder. Other options: a) PCOS -> complex, multifactorial. b) Down’s -> trisomy 21. c) Turner’s -> monosomy X (45, X0). Key point: X-linked -> more severe in males.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: ACE inhibitor are contraindicated in
explanation: Teratogenic in pregnancy -> fetal renal damage. Other options: a) Asthma -> not a contraindication. b) Acute HF -> can be used carefully. d) Diabetic nephropathy -> ACE inhibitors beneficial. Avoid in pregnancy, bilateral RAS, angioedema.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Structure passes through greater sciatic foramen
explanation: Gluteal nerves pass through the greater sciatic foramen to supply gluteal muscles. Other options: Muscles listed do not pass through greater sciatic foramen. foramen. Key point: Sciatic & gluteal nerves traverse greater sciatic foramen.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Antigen presenting cell except
explanation: Neutrophils phagocytose but do not present antigen to T cells. Other options: a) Macrophage -> APC. c) Langerhans cell -> APC. d) Dendritic cell -> best APC. APC = express MHC class II: macrophages, B cells, dendritic cells.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: In secondary hypothyroidism
explanation: Secondary hypothyroidism = pituitary failure -> decreased TSH -> decreased FT4, Key point: Low TSH + Low T4 -> suspect secondary (central).

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Axillary nerve supplies the
explanation: Axillary nerve supplies deltoid & teres minor. Other options: a), (B): Supplied by medial/lateral pectoral nerves. c): Supplied by lower subscapular nerve. deltoid.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Avascular structures include
explanation: Tooth enamel is completely avascular. Other options: b) Highly vascular. c) Vascular connective tissue. d) Retina is vascular. Key point: Enamel = hardest, non-living avascular tissue.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Normal saline is
options: Capable to exert about 300 mosm/L osmotic pressure
explanation: Normal saline = 0.9% NaCl = isotonic to plasma. Other options: a) Close (~308 mOsm/L), but (C) is best. b) Not hypertonic. d) 9 gm/L, not 9 gm meq/L. Key point: Used to correct ECF deficits.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Formation of clot is affected by
explanation: Factor IX -> part of intrinsic coagulation pathway -> affects clot formation.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Continuous capillaries gaseous exchange occurs in
explanation: Lungs have continuous capillaries with tight junctions that allow selective gas exchange while maintaining barrier integrity. Other options: a) Thyroid gland -> fenestrated capillaries. c) Spleen -> sinusoidal capillaries. d) Bone marrow -> sinusoidal capillaries. components but allow gas diffusion.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Causes of short stature include following except
explanation: Klinefelter (XXY) -> tall stature. Why others are incorrect: (A) Psychosocial -> short stature. (B) Hypothyroidism -> short stature. (C) GH deficiency -> short stature. Other causes: Turner, Cushing, skeletal dysplasias.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: DNA viruses are
explanation: Parvovirus is a single-stranded DNA virus, unique among human viral pathogens. Other options: a) Reovirus -> double-stranded RNA virus. b) Picornavirus -> single-stranded RNA virus. c) Orthomyxoviruses -> RNA viruses (influenza). DNA polymerases. Key point: DNA viruses replicate in the nucleus and use host.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Causes of hyperpyrexia
explanation: Malaria - especially falciparum malariacan cause hyperpyrexia (temp > 41 Celsius). Fever follows a cyclical pattern due to schizont rupture. Why others are incorrect: (A) Bronchial asthma -> may have mild fever with infection but not hyperpyrexia. (B) COPD -> may have fever in infective exacerbation, but not hyperpyrexia. Other causes of hyperpyrexia: Heat stroke, Malignant hyperthermia Neuroleptic malignant syndrome, Intracerebral hemorrhage.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Acute renal failure following mismatched blood transfusion is due to
explanation: Mismatched transfusion -> hemolysis -> free hemoglobin -> renal vasoconstriction, tubular necrosis -> ARF. Why others are incorrect: (A) Stricture urethra -> post-renal failure - unrelated. (B) Septicemia can cause ARF but not the main cause in mismatched transfusion. (D) Dehydration worsens ARF but not the primary cause. Related: DIC and hemoglobinuria also contribute to ARF post transfusion reaction.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Continuous capillaries are found in
explanation: Cerebrum and lungs have continuous capillaries with tight junctions -> restrict permeability and allow selective exchange (blood-brain barrier and alveolar capillaries). Other options: b) Liver -> sinusoidal capillaries, highly permeable. d) Pituitary gland -> fenestrated capillaries for hormone exchange. for organ-specific functions.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Common organism for neonatal sepsis
explanation: E. coli is a common cause of early-onset neonatal sepsis. Why others are incorrect: (A) Pneumococci - rare in neonates. (B) Pseudomonas - nosocomial, not common in early sepsis.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: In an immune mediated response, which of the following leukocytes becomes an activated macrophage.
explanation: Monocytes -> macrophages in tissues -> APC, phagocytosis. Other options: a) Lymphocyte -> T/B cells, not macrophages. b) Basophil -> releases histamine. c) Neutrophils -> remain neutrophils. Key point: Monocyte -> macrophage is key for innate immunity.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Omega 3 essential fatty acid are
explanation: Linoleic acid (LA) is an essential fatty acid; omega-6, but precursor to omega-3 pathway. Other options: b) Carbonic acid -> not a fatty acid. c) Arachidonic acid -> omega-6. d) Oleic acid -> omega-9. Omega-3 FAs (ALA, EPA, DHA) -> anti-inflammatory effects.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Testosterone is synthesised from
explanation: Testosterone is a steroid hormone synthesized from cholesterol via enzymatic pathways in Leydig cells. Other options: b) Glycine -> amino acid, c) Oestrogen -> derived from testosterone, not precursor. d) Tyrosine -> precursor for catecholamines,

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Following predispose to the development of tuberculosis
explanation: Malnutrition impairs cell-mediated immunity -> increases susceptibility to tuberculosis infection and reactivation. Other options: a) HLA-B27 -> associated with autoimmune diseases, not TB predisposition. b) Sarcoidosis -> granulomatous disease mimicking TB, but not a risk factor.

subject: 42nd Special BCS
heading: 42nd Special BCS
stem: Polycythemia occurs in
explanation: Hypoxia stimulates erythropoietin production -> increased RBC production -> polycythemia. Other options: b) Iron deficiency -> causes anemia, not polycythemia. c) Vitamin C deficiency -> affects collagen, not RBC production. d) Malnutrition -> usually causes anemia. chronic low oxygen states. Key point: Secondary polycythemia is an adaptive response to hypoxia. 39th Special BCS

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Modifiable risk factor of hypertension is
explanation: Smoking = modifiable risk factor (lifestyle changeable). Incorrect: Age, sex, family history -> non-modifiable.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Causes of bilateral leg swelling does not always include
explanation: DVT usually -> unilateral swelling. Other options: a), (b), (c) -> common causes of bilateral swelling.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: RK-39 strip test is used to diagnose
explanation: RK-39 -> rapid diagnostic test for visceral leishmaniasis (Kala-azar). Other options: Not used for malaria, dengue,

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Dermis
options: Is a layer of epithelial tissue
Is formed by connective tissue 39th Special BCS
explanation: Dermis = collagen, elastin, fibroblasts -> connective tissue layer. Other options: a) Epithelial -> epidermis. c) Melanocytes -> basal layer of epidermis. d) Keratinocytes -> epidermis; Extra info: Epidermis (epithelial) vs Dermis (connective tissue).

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which of the following structure passes through the aortic opening of the diaphragm?
explanation: The aortic hiatus transmits the aorta, thoracic duct, and azygos vein. Thoracic duct passes here specifically. Incorrect: Inferior vena cava passes through the caval opening. Vagal trunks pass through the esophageal hiatus.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Ovulation occurs
options: 14 days after the onset of menstruation
14 days before the onset of next menstruation

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which of the following malignancies is associated with radiation?
explanation: Ionizing radiation -> DNA damage -> ALL risk increased.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which vitamin is not synthesized in body?
explanation: Vitamin A must be obtained from diet. Other options: Vit D: skin synthesis. Vit K, Biotin: gut flora.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Following are the causes of vertigo except
explanation: Bell’s palsy is a facial nerve palsy causing facial weakness, not vertigo. Benign positional vertigo, acoustic neuroma, vestibular neuritis all cause vertigo.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Extra pyramidal lesion causes
explanation: Cogwheel rigidity -> hallmark of basal ganglia lesion (extrapyramidal). Other options: a) Flaccid paralysis -> LMN. b) Hyperkinesia -> may occur but not specific. d) Hyperreflexia -> UMN.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: BCG vaccine at birth causes
explanation: BCG -> induces controlled local TB infection -> cell- mediated immunity. Other options: Does NOT prevent primary/secondary TB or MDR TB.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Superior mesentric artery supplies blood to
explanation: SMA -> ileocolic artery -> appendix. Other options: a) 1st part of duodenum -> celiac trunk. b) Left 1/3 of transverse colon -> inferior mesenteric artery. c) Gall bladder -> cystic artery (from hepatic artery).

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: During sleep, there is fall in the circulating level of hormone except
explanation: Growth hormone secretion increases during sleep, especially deep sleep. Adrenaline, cortisol, and insulin levels generally fall during sleep.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Commonest cause of hepatic cirrhosis in Bangladesh is
explanation: HBV infection is highly prevalent in Bangladesh and a leading cause of cirrhosis. Other options: a) HAV -> causes acute hepatitis, no chronicity. c) HCV -> common in West, but less in Bangladesh. d) HEV -> acute infection, not chronic cirrhosis; Extra info: Screening for HBV is done by HBsAg. Anti IgG HBV - Chronic infection & Anti IgM HBV - acute infection Hepatitis E virus causes fulminant hepatitis in pregnancy.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: In infants, defecation often follows a meal. The cause of colonic contractions in the situation is
explanation: The gastrocolic reflex is a normal response where food in the stomach triggers colonic contractions leading to defecation.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which of the following condition is not precancerous?
explanation: GSD -> metabolic disease, not linked to malignancy. Other options: a) Solar keratosis -> SCC risk. b) Ulcerative colitis -> colon CA. c) Cervical dysplasia -> cervical CA.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Plasma clearance value of glucose is
explanation: Glucose is completely reabsorbed in the renal tubules, so its plasma clearance is essentially zero in healthy kidneys.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which one of the following is responsible for carpal tunnel syndrome?
explanation: Compression of median nerve in carpal tunnel -> pain, numbness, weakness in hand. Extra info: Phalen, Tinel’s signs positive in CTS.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Clinical cyanosis is due to
explanation: Cyanosis when reduced Hb > 5g/dL -> blue discoloration. Other options: a) Adult Hb -> normal, not cause. c) Fetal Hb -> not cause. d) Biliverdin -> pigment, not cyanosis; Extra info: Central cyanosis = hypoxemia Peripheral cyanosis = sluggish circulation.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Karyotype of T urner Syndrome is
explanation: Turner syndrome -> missing one X chromosome -> 45 XO. Incorrect: 45 XY = male. 46 XX = normal female. 47 XXY = Klinefelter’s.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Clinical toxicity occurs in all of the following micro nutrients except
explanation: Iodine toxicity is rare, body regulates iodine balance well. Excess usually excreted. Toxicity of iron, fluoride, copper is more common clinically. Other options: a) Iron -> iron overload -> hemosiderosis, hemochromatosis. c) Fluoride -> dental/skeletal fluorosis. d) Copper -> Wilson’s disease (toxic copper accumulation) 39th Special BCS

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which one of the following clotting factor is called primary clotting factor?
explanation: Fibrinogen (Factor I) -> primary substrate -> converted to fibrin -> clot. Other options: b) Stable factor (Factor VII) -> extrinsic pathway. c) Labile factor (Factor V) -> cofactor. d) Antehemophilic (Factor VIII) -> intrinsic pathway; Extra info: Fibrin mesh stabilizes clot.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: The major patho physiologic abnormality of Dengue Shock Syndrome is
explanation: Dengue Shock Syndrome is characterized by increased vascular permeability leading to plasma leakage and hypovolemia.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Compared to hepatic bile, gall bladder bile Glucose contains a reduced concentration of which of the following?
explanation: Gall bladder bile is concentrated by absorption of water and electrolytes; therefore, water concentration is reduced compared to hepatic bile.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Amount of Hb contained in late normoblast is
explanation: Late normoblast (orthochromatic normoblast) contains approximately 30 picograms of Hb.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: In progressive phase of shock
options: There is wide spread tissue hypoxia
explanation: Progressive shock -> impaired perfusion -> tissue hypoxia -> lactic acidosis. Other options: a) Survival still possible if treated. b) Renal shutdown not complete yet. c) Causes metabolic acidosis not alkalosis.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Autonomic ganglion are
explanation: Preganglionic fibers release acetylcholine -> cholinergic. Other options: Adrenergic/noradrenergic apply to postganglionic sympathetic only.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Blood group antigens are
options: Present in the dense granules of platelets
explanation: ABO blood group antigens are glycoproteins/glycolipids on RBC membranes. Other options: a) Hb -> inside RBC, . b) Platelet granules -> unrelated. d) Plasma -> antibodies, not antigens; Extra info: Blood grouping based on antigens on RBCs + antibodies in plasma.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Cardinal feature of atopic dermatitis is
explanation: Intense itching -> scratching -> eczema cycle. Other options: Swelling, oily skin, increased IgM -> not primary features.

subject: 39th Special BCS

stem: Serum sodium level is
explanation: Normal range: 135-145 mmol/L.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which one of the following is a source of pulmonary embolism?
explanation: Most PEs originate from deep vein thrombosis (DVT) of legs (femoral, popliteal veins). Other options: a), (b), (d) -> uncommon/rare sources;

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Drug used in “Scabies” is
explanation: Permethrin cream is the first-line topical treatment for scabies.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Cardiogenic shock may be due to
explanation: Pump failure (MI, arrhythmia, cardiomyopathy) -> decreased cardiac output -> cardiogenic shock. Other options: b) Infection -> septic shock. c) Hypovolemia -> hypovolemic shock. d) Neurogenic -> vasodilation; Key features of cardiogenic shock: low BP , high JVP , pulmonary edema.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Milk ejection in female is caused by
explanation: Oxytocin -> milk ejection reflex (myoepithelial cell contraction). Incorrect: Prolactin -> milk production, not ejection. Estrogen/progesterone -> inhibit lactation during pregnancy.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Immediate blood transfusion reaction includes
explanation: Air embolism -> rapid/immediate complication during transfusion. Other options: b) Hypercalcemia, (c) Hypokalemia: rare or delayed. d) Circulatory overload -> can be immediate but usually develops over time.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Extracellular structural protein is
explanation: Elastin -> ECM protein for tissue elasticity. Incorrect: Keratin = intracellular structural protein. Tubulin = cytoskeletal protein. Gastrin = hormone.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which of the following types of shock is caused by failure of the heart to pump effectively?
explanation: Cardiogenic shock = failure of pump -> decreased CO. Other options: a) Septic -> vasodilation. c) Hypovolemic -> low volume. d) Anaphylactic -> vasodilation.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Medial surface of brain is supplied by
explanation: ACA supplies medial surface of frontal/parietal lobes. Other options: a) MCA -> lateral surface. c) Vertebral -> brainstem/posterior brain. d) PICA -> cerebellum/medulla.

subject: 39th Special BCS

explanation: Epiphyseal plate -> hyaline cartilage. Other options: Auditory tube, epiglottis, auricle -> elastic cartilage.

Has a lining of stratified squamous epithelium
Is related anteriorly to the cervix
Has a venous drainage into the superior vena cava

subject: 39th Special BCS

stem: Prednisolone 5 mg is equivalent to
explanation: Steroid equivalence: Hydrocortisone 20 mg about Prednisolone 5 mg. Other options: a) 40 mg -> too high. c) Dexamethasone 2 mg -> too strong. d) Dexamethasone 8 mg -> very high;

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Erythroblastosis fetalis may develop when
explanation: Rh-negative mother exposed to Rh-positive fetal blood -> sensitization -> next pregnancy -> hemolysis. Other options: Other combinations do not trigger maternal immune reaction. Extra info: Prevented by anti-D immunoglobulin postpartum.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Nephrotic syndrome includes
explanation: Nephrotic syndrome = massive proteinuria (>3.5 g/day), hypoalbuminemia, edema, hyperlipidemia. Other options: a) Hematuria -> seen in nephritic syndrome. b) Hypertension -> may occur but not defining. c) Oliguria -> not classic feature.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which disease is the not mimicking anxiety disorder?
explanation: Hypothyroidism causes depression, fatigue, not typically anxiety symptoms. Incorrect: Alcohol withdrawal, hypoglycemia, and temporal lobe epilepsy can mimic anxiety symptoms.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Adult polycystic kidney disease is a condition of
explanation: ADPKD -> autosomal dominant, PKD1/ PKD2 mutations. Other options: Not X-linked, recessive, or chromosomal abnormality. Extra info: Presents with hypertension, renal failure, cysts.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: At which of the following phase of cardiac cycle does the atrioventricular valve open?
explanation: AV valves open during ventricular diastole -> blood flows into ventricles..

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: The drug of choice for cerebral malaria is
explanation: WHO recommends IV artesunate for cerebral malaria (fast acting, life saving). Other options: Oral quinine: slower, used when IV unavailable. Doxycycline, sulfamethoxazole + pyrimethamine: adjunctive, not first-line for cerebral malaria.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: The supporting cells of nervous system is called
explanation: Neuroglia (glial cells) support, protect, and nourish neurons.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: A 60 year old gentleman has been diagnosed as vitamin B12 deficiency due to pernicious anemia. Which of the following is unlikely to happen?
explanation: B12 deficiency causes posterior column, corticospinal damage; seizures are rare. Other options: a), (c), (d) -> neurological features of B12 deficiency.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Basal cell carcinoma includes
options: Typically at the non sun exposure
Early lesions of pale translucent papules
explanation: BCC -> locally invasive, rarely metastasizes. Other options: b) Occurs on sun-exposed skin. c) RB gene not typically involved. d) Lesion: pearly papule.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Histamin causes
explanation: Histamine -> vasodilatation via H1 receptors -> hypotension, edema. Other options: a) Hypertension -> opposite. b) Vasoconstriction -> wrong. d) Bradycardia -> reflex tachycardia often occurs; Extra info: Histamine key mediator in anaphylaxis.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Morphological appearance of necrosis is the result of
explanation: Denatured proteins + enzyme digestion -> necrosis morphology. Other options: Saponification -> fat necrosis. Mummification -> dry gangrene (late). Alkalosis: unrelated.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Causes of renal failure in multiple myeloma includes all except
explanation: Hypercalcemia (not hypo) is common in MM -> renal dysfunction. Other options: a) Membranous GN. b) Paraprotein deposition -> light chains (Bence Jones) toxic to kidney. d) Amyloid deposition -> causes renal impairment; Extra info: “Myeloma kidney” due to light chain nephropathy.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which of the following is a tumor marker?
explanation: CA 19-9 -> tumor marker for pancreatic, biliary cancers. Incorrect: PSA = for prostate cancer (also tumor marker, but not option B). CRP = inflammation marker. Ferritin = iron stores.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: The tissue macrophage is derived from
explanation: Circulating monocytes -> tissue -> differentiate to macrophages. Other options: Lymphocytes, eosinophils, helper T cells -> different lineage.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Features of fibroadenoma include
explanation: Actually, fibroadenoma is most common in women under 30. Most correct feature should be “usually single, mobile, painless mass” in younger women as C is the closest option here it is marked as correct.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Extracellular matrix is more in
explanation: ECM most abundant in connective tissue -> collagen, proteoglycans, etc. Other options: a) Nervous -> neurons/glial cells. b) Epithelial -> minimal ECM (basement membrane). c) Muscle -> mainly cellular.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: The value of lung tidal volume is
explanation: Normal tidal volume = ~500 ml per breath.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Abnormal constituent of urine is
explanation: Albumin should not be present -> indicates glomerular pathology. Other options: a) Creatinine -> normal. b) Urea -> normal. c) Phosphate -> normal;

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which component is not present in CSF?
explanation: Normal CSF -> no RBCs. RBCs suggest pathology (bleed, trauma). Other options: Glucose, protein, leucocytes -> normal small amounts present.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Non cardiac causes of atrial fibrillation is
explanation: Pneumonia and other lung diseases can cause atrial fibrillation due to hypoxia and systemic stress. Chronic liver disease, kidney disease, and stroke are less commonly direct causes.

Is a progressive inflammatory disorder of the arterial
Involves only some blood vessels of body

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: In adult, the daily loss of fluid in the feces, normally is
explanation: Normal daily fecal water loss is about 100 ml; more than this can indicate diarrhea.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which of the following occurs during reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction?
explanation: RT-PCR -> converts RNA -> complementary DNA (cDNA) -> amplified.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: The superficial inguinal ring is an opening in the
explanation: The superficial inguinal ring is a triangular opening in the external oblique aponeurosis through which the spermatic cord (in males) or round ligament (in females) passes. Other options: a) Internal oblique aponeurosis -> Forms part of the inguinal canal wall, but does not form the superficial ring. b) Conjoint tendon -> Strengthens the posterior wall of the inguinal canal, unrelated to the superficial ring. d) Fascia transversalis -> Forms the deep inguinal ring, not the superficial one. Extra info: Deep inguinal ring: Opening in transversalis fascia Superficial inguinal ring: Opening in external oblique aponeurosis.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: All are functions of epithelial tissue except
explanation: Epithelial tissue performs absorption, secretion, and some contractility in specialized cells, but globulin synthesis is a function of plasma cells (immune cells), not epithelial tissue.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Medial boundary of the femoral ring is formed by
explanation: The femoral ring is bounded medially by the lacunar ligament, laterally by the femoral vein, anteriorly by the inguinal ligament, and posteriorly by the pectineus muscle.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Acute heart failure may occur in
explanation: Myxedema (severe hypothyroidism) can cause acute heart failure due to decreased cardiac contractility and output.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Ghon Focus is situated in
explanation: Ghon focus = primary lesion of TB in lung parenchyma (often subpleural, midzone). Other options: a), (b), (c) -> Not sites for Ghon focus. Extra info: Ghon complex = Ghon focus + affected hilar nodes.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Microcytic hypochromic anemia is found in
explanation: Thalassemia -> defective Hb synthesis -> microcytic, hypochromic anemia. Other options: a), (b), (d) -> cause normocytic or other types of anemia.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Confirmatory marker for Viremic stage of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is
explanation: HBV DNA = direct marker of active viral replication (viremia). Incorrect: HBsAg = surface antigen, not viral load. Anti-HBs = immunity. Anti-HBc IgG = past infection.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which of the following crosses the ureter in the female as it approaches the ureterovesical junction?
explanation: Uterine artery crosses ureter anteriorly -> “water (ureter) under the bridge (uterine artery).”. Other options: a) Ovarian artery -> crosses higher. c) Obturator nerve -> unrelated. d) Internal iliac -> distant;.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Male external genital organ includes
explanation: Penis = external genital organ. Incorrect: Seminal vesicle, epididymis, prostate -> internal genital structures.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Mycobacterium leprae has special predilection for
explanation: M. leprae -> Schwann cells -> nerve damage. Other options: Epithelium, lymphatics, dorsal-root ganglion -> not primary target.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which of the following types of necrosis is seen in acute myocardial infarction?
explanation: MI leads to ischemia -> hypoxia -> denaturation of proteins -> coagulative necrosis (preserved architecture with loss of nuclei). Other options: a) Caseous -> Found in TB infections. b) Gangrenous -> Applied to gross tissue with necrosis plus bacterial infection. d) Fat -> Seen in pancreatitis (fat saponification); Extra info: Coagulative necrosis = hallmark of ischemic injury in solid organs (heart, kidney). Brain = liquefactive necrosis in ischemia.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Parasitic infection associated with anemia is
explanation: Necator americanus (hookworm) causes blood loss anemia by attaching to intestinal mucosa. Incorrect: Loa loa, Wuchereria bancrofti, Onchocerca -> cause filariasis, not anemia.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Detrusor muscle is a muscle of
explanation: Detrusor muscle forms the muscular layer of the bladder wall, responsible for contraction during urination.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Exotoxin mediated disease is
explanation: Streptococcus pyogenes exotoxins -> tissue necrosis. Other options: Wegener’s granulomatosis -> autoimmune. Kuru, Nipah -> prion/viral, no exotoxins.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Christmas disease develops due to deficiency of clotting factor
explanation: Christmas disease = Hemophilia B, caused by factor IX deficiency. Incorrect: Factor VIII deficiency causes Hemophilia A. Factors V and VII are unrelated.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which of the following may cause hypercalcaemia?
explanation: Multiple myeloma -> bone destruction -> increased serum calcium. Other options: b) Furosemide -> promotes calciuresis -> lowers calcium. c) Hypoparathyroidism -> hypocalcemia. d) Cushing’s -> usually not hypercalcemia;

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Insulin increases
explanation: Insulin promotes glucose storage -> glycogenesis. Other options: a) Lipolysis -> inhibited. b) Ketogenesis -> inhibited. d) Gluconeogenesis -> inhibited;

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: X-linked recessive disorder is
explanation: Hemophilia A and B are classic X-linked recessive disorders. Incorrect: Alkaptonuria, polycystic kidney disease, Wilson’s disease are autosomal.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: During accommodation reaction there is
options: Constriction of pupil by sympathetic nerve
Increase in transverse diameter of lens
explanation: Ciliary muscle contraction -> lens curvature increased -> near focus.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: DNA is found in
explanation: DNA is packaged into chromosomes. Incorrect: Golgi, ribosome, lysosome -> no DNA.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Simple squamous epithelium is found in
explanation: Endothelium -> simple squamous -> allows exchange. Other options: Gall bladder -> columnar. Urinary bladder -> transitional. Fallopian tube -> ciliated columnar.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Which one of the following acts as antioxidant?
explanation: Ceruloplasmin -> copper-binding protein -> antioxidant role. Other options: b) Ionizing radiation, (c) H2O2, (d) Hypochlorous acid -> pro-oxidants.

subject: 39th Special BCS
heading: 39th Special BCS
stem: Pre XDR tuberculosis means: pyrazinamide
options: TB resistant to isoniazid and rifampicin

explanation: The face lacks deep fascia -> allows free movement of facial muscles (mimicry). Other options: a) Sole -> has dense plantar fascia. c) Neck -> has investing layer of deep cervical fascia. d) Abdominal wall -> has fascia transversalis; Extra info: Superficial fascia only in face -> allows expression.

explanation: In UMN lesion: reflexes are increased, not lost. Loss of reflexes -> LMN lesion. explanation: Arterioles (resistance vessels) control blood flow and systemic vascular resistance through smooth muscle tone. Other options: b) Metarteriole -> transitional vessels. c) Venule -> capacitance vessels, low resistance. d) Capillary -> low resistance, mainly exchange of gases/nutrients; Extra info: Systemic BP mainly controlled by arteriolar tone (SNS, hormones).
